                                    DRAFT PRELIMINARY ORDER

       Southwestern Electric Power Company (SWEPCO) filed an application for authority to
amend its tariffs for retail service to include a new standard form contract for Electric Service –
Large Load (ES-LL Contract) customers. This preliminary order identifies the issues that must be
addressed in this proceeding.

       SWEPCO proposed for the new standard form contract to apply to any customer with a
contract capacity of 75 or more megawatts.1 According to SWEPCO, “the proposed ES-LL
Contract will help ensure the collection of revenue from large customers cover the costs associated
with developing the infrastructure necessary to serve these large loads while protecting existing
customers from the risks associated with developing the infrastructure necessary to serve these
large loads.”2 Because potential large-load customers are seeking certainty, SWEPCO requests
that the Commission expedite processing the application.3

       SWEPCO filed the application on October 3, 2025. To date, Docket Management has
granted motions to intervene filed by Texas Industrial Energy Consumers and the Office of Public
Utility Counsel (OPUC).4 On November 18, 2025, Cities Advocating Reasonable Deregulation
filed a late motion to intervene that has not yet been ruled on.




       1
           Direct Testimony of Melissa A. Gage at 12 (Oct. 3, 2025).
       2
           Application at 3 (Oct. 3, 2025).
       3
           Id.
       4
           Order No. 2 (Oct. 29, 2025).
 PUC Docket No. 58796                        Draft Preliminary Order                       Page 2 of 4


       SWEPCO was directed, and Commission Staff and other interested persons were allowed,
by November 25, 2025 to file a list of issues to be addressed in the docket and also identify any
issues not to be addressed and any threshold legal or policy issues that should be addressed.
SWEPCO, Commission Staff, and OPUC each timely filed a list of issues.


                                    I.         Issues to be Addressed
       The Commission must provide to the administrative law judge (ALJ) a list of issues or
areas to be addressed in any proceeding referred to the State Office of Administrative Hearings
(SOAH).5 After reviewing the pleadings submitted by the parties, the Commission identifies the
following issues that must be addressed in this docket:

1. Is this the appropriate type of proceeding for the relief sought by SWEPCO? Should the
   Commission instead require any such relief to be sought in a base-rate proceeding?

2. Is the application administratively complete?

3. Did SWEPCO provide sufficient notice of the application?

4. Has SWEPCO complied with the applicable requirements of 16 Texas Administrative Code
   § 25.241?

5. Should the Commission approve SWEPCO’s proposed tariff?
   a. Should the Commission approve the proposed standard form contract for ES-LL Contract
       customers?

   b. Are the proposed terms and conditions of service for large-load customers reasonable?

   c. Does SWEPCO’s proposal adequately address the effects, if any, on SWEPCO’s other
       customers, including residential and small commercial customers?

       This list of issues is not intended to be exhaustive. The parties and the ALJ are free to raise
and address any issues relevant in this docket that they deem necessary, subject to any limitations
imposed by the ALJ or by the Commission in future orders issued in this docket. The Commission
may identify and provide to the ALJ in the future any additional issues or areas that must be
addressed, as permitted under Texas Government Code § 2003.049(e).

       5
           Tex. Gov’t Code § 2003.049(e).
 PUC Docket No. 58796                 Draft Preliminary Order                            Page 3 of 4


                             II.      Effect of Preliminary Order
       This Order is preliminary in nature and is entered without prejudice to any party expressing
views contrary to this Order before the SOAH ALJ at hearing. The SOAH ALJ, upon his or her
own motion or upon the motion of any party, may deviate from this Order when circumstances
dictate that it is reasonable to do so. Any ruling by the SOAH ALJ that deviates from this Order
may be appealed to the Commission. The Commission will not address whether this Order should
be modified except upon its own motion or the appeal of a SOAH ALJ’s order. Furthermore, this
Order is not subject to motions for rehearing or reconsideration.
